bug_semantics: CWE-918: isPrivateIP in kernel/util/net.go, used by SSRFSafeDialer under SafeMode, only treated loopback, link-local unicast, RFC1918/ULA private, and unspecified addresses as blocked. It did not unwrap IPv6 transition embeddings (NAT64 64:ff9b::/96, 6to4 2002::/16, Teredo 2001::/32) that carry private IPv4 destinations. An authenticated caller of the network forward / WebSocket / SSE proxy endpoints can supply a hostname that resolves to such an address and reach internal services or cloud metadata (e.g. 169.254.169.254). The forward proxy returns the response body, so this is full-read SSRF.
flaw_origin: First write of SSRFSafeDialer plus isPrivateIP in PR #17748. The helper was authored as ip.IsLoopback() || ip.IsLinkLocalUnicast() || ip.IsPrivate() || ip.IsUnspecified() with no transition-prefix unwrap, and was wired immediately into the kernel proxy dialers. That incomplete predicate is the advisory sink; later IPv6-transition patches on other helpers are not this first write.
evidence: CVE-2026-74905 is PUBLISHED on cve.org (GHSA-qrjw-gxw5-x7q9 withdrawn_at null); CNA title matches IPv6 transition bypass in isPrivateIP, affected < 3.7.4, patched in 3.7.4. Repo advisory referenced by the CVE is GHSA-qq8m-8p8v-x4xg. Direct fix ecdf6038054dcd60da7cbbf6622c2863843612f0 (author/committer Daniel 845765@qq.com) expands isPrivateIP to also block multicast/link-local multicast and recursively unwrap NAT64/6to4/Teredo embedded IPv4. git log -S "func isPrivateIP" -- kernel/util/net.go first hits dda0fb91367ad6c523a72e5dfd4ceb88c04a9699 (:art: Add Generic Streamed Proxy Responses for Kernel Plugins #17748). That commit adds SSRFSafeDialer Control hook calling isPrivateIP and the four-predicate helper. git cat-file -e 899b8c6eb3580a346360a4d0b27c0b99a527a0ea:kernel/util/net.go succeeds; git grep for func isPrivateIP / SSRFSafeDialer on the parent path exits 1 (parent has only an unrelated IPv4 IsPrivate check). git log --all --grep=#17748 shows only this GitHub squash; no finer public members. BIC author mm-o fly.x@outlook.com, committer GitHub noreply@github.com; commit object has no Co-Authored-By / Generated-with / bot author. Later a8d2cc4e4 / dd2778b70 are other SSRF sinks/follow-ups, not the first write of this helper. ppa re-checked line-level 2026-08-29: git show 899b8c6e:kernel/util/net.go has no SSRFSafeDialer or isPrivateIP (its only IsPrivate match, line 89, is the unrelated LAN-address collector); the BIC dda0fb91 adds both functions with the stdlib-only predicate missing NAT64/6to4/Teredo coverage. -> introducer_parent_absent=true.
reasoning: The advisory is a real, published CWE-918 in the SafeMode SSRF dialer. The vulnerable lines are the original isPrivateIP body, first written in dda0fb913 and absent from the verifiable parent tree. That squash is the smallest surviving public object.
